title: swf-generation-supreme-world-heavyweight
label: Jack Bruce

won.source: The diary's own later posts: "since winning the SWF World Heavyweight title back in August" (the Fry Report preview posted 7 October 2008) and "the first time since last August when Bruce won the belt" (in-game March 2008).

how: Jack Bruce's reign as the diary opens: the diary's later posts date it from last August, and Bruce says he took the belt from Runaway Train; he keeps it through Brandon James at Awesome Impact and Remo at The World is Watching. His later posts: Bruce beats Vengeance in a Supreme Cell match at Master of Puppets 2008, beats Eric Eisen at Times of Trouble 2008, beats Antonio Marquez and John McClean on Supreme TV in Week 3 of June and Jay Chord in Week 2 of July 2008, and is booked for Supreme Double Jeopardy at The Supreme Challenge 28. He beat Eric Tyler and Vengeance in the first Supreme Double Jeopardy match at The Supreme Challenge 28, then lost the belt to Rich Money in the second, ending a reign the SWF.com review puts at some eleven months.

title: swf-generation-supreme-north-american
label: Steve Frehley

won.source: The World is Watching, Thursday, Week 2, April 2008 (in-game); the vacating is Supreme TV, Tuesday, Week 3, April 2008.

how: Won in a no-disqualification, no-count-out match against Rich Money at The World is Watching; Frehley then lays the belt down in the ring on Supreme TV, refusing to defend it, and Richard Eisen takes it away.

title: swf-generation-supreme-north-american
label: Marc DuBois

won.source: Master of Puppets 2008, Thursday, Week 2, May 2008 (in-game).

how: Won the eight-man Grand Prix for the vacant title by beating Rocky Golden in the semi final and Eric Eisen in the final at Master of Puppets 2008; kept it against Thom Barrowman on Supreme TV in Week 3 of May, against Elmo Benson on the first SWF Legends and against Remo, by count-out, on Supreme TV in Week 2 of June 2008. He kept it in a three-way against Runaway Train and Antonio Marquez at Times of Trouble 2008, against Valiant on Supreme TV in Week 4 of June and, when Chris Morrisette won by disqualification for a belt shot, on Supreme TV in Week 1 of July 2008. He kept it at The Supreme Challenge 28 in a Threefold Threat against Zimmy Bumfhole and Antonio Marquez, when Darryl Devine's interference let him throw the referee in front of Marquez's shooting star press and pin Bumfhole, and is booked for another Threefold Threat at Welcome to the Jungle 2008. He kept it in the Threefold Threat at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 when Darryl Devine tapped to the Model Solution sleeper, beat Zimmy Bumfhole on Supreme TV in Week 4 of August 2008 and Scout of The New Wave in Week 1 of September, and is billed against Art Reed in Week 2.

title: swf-generation-supreme-world-tag-team
label: Sexual Aggression

won.source: The diary's set-up post ("The only title change was Sexual Aggression winning the tag titles in February") and its TEW.com monthly report for February 2008.

how: Sexual Aggression took the belts from The Amazing Bumfholes at Nothing to Lose in February 2008, then defends them on Supreme TV, at Awesome Impact and at The World is Watching. They lost the belts to Valiant & Giedroyc on the first SWF Legends in Week 1 of June 2008, after Joe Sexy walked out on Angry Gilmore.

title: swf-generation-supreme-shooting-star
label: Darryl Devine

won.source: The World is Watching, Thursday, Week 2, April 2008 (in-game).

how: Won in a ladder match against Marc DuBois at The World is Watching, and kept against Mainstream Hernandez on Generation Supreme on Friday, Week 3, April 2008. He kept it in the three-way ladder match at Times of Trouble 2008 and lost it to Kid Toma on SWF Legends in June 2008, when Akima Brave and BJ O'Neill distracted the referee and Toma, Akima and Tana used a chair.

title: swf-generation-supreme-shooting-star
label: Kid Toma

won.source: SWF Legends, in-game June 2008 (the post's own heading reads "Wednesday, Week 1, June 2008"; the Fry Report posts either side of it place the show in Week 3).

how: Won the belt from Darryl Devine on SWF Legends in June 2008 after Akima Brave and BJ O'Neill distracted the referee and Toma, Akima and Tana used a chair on the champion; kept it against Brett Biggz and American Elemental on SWF Legends in Week 4 of June and against Jacob Jett on SWF Legends in Week 2 of July 2008. He kept it against Remmy Skye on SWF Legends in Week 4 of July 2008, the night Eric Tyler handed him a redesigned belt; Bart Biggz earned a shot at the Welcome to the Jungle 2008 pay-per-view by beating Akima Brave by disqualification in Week 1 of August. He lost it to Acid in a Threefold Threat with Bart Biggz at Welcome to the Jungle 2008, Acid pinning him.
note: The post for this SWF Legends show reads "Wednesday, Week 2, July 2008" in its own heading; the Fry Report preview posted before it ("Wednesday, Week 4, July 2008") and the shows either side of it place it in Week 4, and this record follows them.

title: swf-generation-supreme-generations
label: Ace Newton

won.source: The World is Watching, Thursday, Week 2, April 2008 (in-game).

how: The first champion, who won the belt by eliminating Robbie Retro last in a ten-man battle royal at The World is Watching and kept it against Gino Montero on Generation Supreme on Friday, Week 3, April 2008. He lost it to Robbie Retro on Supreme TV in Week 1 of June 2008.

title: swf-generation-supreme-north-american
label: Rich Money

won.source: The diary opens with Rich Money as North American champion (Supreme TV, Tuesday, Week 1, March 2008); it does not date the win; dates are the diary's own in-game dates.

how: Rich Money's reign as the diary opens; the diary does not say when he won it. He keeps it against Eric Tyler, Randy Bumfhole and Christian Faith and loses it to Steve Frehley at The World is Watching.

title: swf-generation-supreme-generations
label: Robbie Retro
how: Won the belt from Ace Newton on Supreme TV in Week 1 of June 2008 with Murder on the Dance Floor and kept it against Paul Huntingdon on Supreme TV in Week 2 of June 2008. He kept it against Sean Deeley on Supreme TV in Week 1 of July 2008. He kept it against Ash Campbell on Supreme TV in Week 3 of July 2008 and lost it to Ace Newton in a Threefold Threat with Jay Chord on Supreme TV in Week 4.

title: swf-generation-supreme-world-tag-team
label: Valiant & Giedroyc
how: Won the belts from Sexual Aggression on the first SWF Legends, when Joe Sexy walked out on Angry Gilmore mid-match and Giedroyc pinned Gilmore, and kept them against Last Chance on SWF Legends in Week 2 of June 2008. They kept them in the four-way at Times of Trouble 2008 when Giedroyc's stoppage win ended it, then against The Heartbreakers on Supreme TV in Week 1 of July and The Upper Class on Supreme TV in Week 2 of July 2008. They kept them at The Supreme Challenge 28 in a Threefold Threat against The New Wave and Badd Kompany, when Valiant pinned Joss Thompson, and are booked against Sin Inc for Welcome to the Jungle 2008. They kept them at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 against Sin Inc, when Giedroyc rolled up John McClean, against The Upper Class on Supreme TV in Week 3 of August 2008 and against The Heartbreakers in Week 1 of September; Richard Eisen names The New Wave the next challengers.

title: swf-generation-supreme-legends
label: Chris Caufield
how: The first champion, who won the four-way elimination match for the belt on the first SWF Legends, eliminating John McClean, then Runaway Train, and wore it to the ring in his non-title match with Eric Eisen on SWF Legends in Week 2 of June 2008. He kept it against Enygma on SWF Legends in June 2008, against Texas Pete, by count-out, on SWF Legends in Week 4 of June and against Enforcer Roberts on SWF Legends in Week 2 of July 2008. He lost it to Bloodstone at The Supreme Challenge 28, the referee stopping the match in the camel clutch while Caufield insisted he had not submitted.

title: swf-generation-supreme-shooting-star
label: Acid

won.source: Welcome to the Jungle 2008, in-game Week 2 of August 2008 (post #467).

how: Won the belt from Kid Toma in a Threefold Threat with Bart Biggz at Welcome to the Jungle 2008, on his first night in the SWF's big shows, pinning Toma after the Acid Rain Bomb swandive senton. He kept it against El Leon and Mainstream Hernandez on SWF Legends in Week 3 of August 2008, against Remmy Skye by submission in Week 4 and against John Greed and Mainstream Hernandez in Week 1 of September; Bart Biggz asks for a one-on-one match for it.

title: swf-generation-supreme-world-heavyweight
label: Rich Money

won.source: The Supreme Challenge 28, in-game Week 2 of July 2008 (post #300).

how: Won the title from Jack Bruce in the second Supreme Double Jeopardy match at The Supreme Challenge 28: out of the first match after a disqualification loss to Randy Bumfhole, he came down the ramp in a suit and took it off piece by piece while Richard Eisen hesitated, and pinned Bruce after his finisher. He says the belt will be defended only on pay-per-view, makes Bruce and Randy Bumfhole each beat Remo for a shot, beats Valiant in a non-title match on Supreme TV in Week 4 of July 2008, replaces the belt with a black one set with diamonds, and is booked in a Threefold Threat with Bruce and Bumfhole at Welcome to the Jungle 2008. He kept it at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 in a Threefold Threat against Jack Bruce and Randy Bumfhole, pinning Bruce, and against Guide of The New Wave on Supreme TV in Week 3 of August 2008; on a video he turned down Bruce's challenge for Under Control 2008, and Pistol Pete Hall is billed against him for the belt on Supreme TV in Week 2 of September.

title: swf-generation-supreme-supreme
label: Christian Faith

won.source: The Supreme Challenge 28, in-game Week 2 of July 2008 (post #300).

how: The first champion, who beat Brandon James with the Test of Faith sleeper at The Supreme Challenge 28 and received the belt from Phil Vibert. He kept it in a Threefold Threat against Bloodstone and Eric Eisen on SWF Legends in Week 3 of July 2008, against Troy Tornado on SWF Legends in Week 4 of July and against Texas Pete on SWF Legends in Week 1 of August 2008, and is booked against Vengeance for Welcome to the Jungle 2008. He beat Vengeance at Welcome to the Jungle 2008, after which Vengeance put him through the timekeeper's table, beat Bryan Holmes on SWF Legends in Week 3 of August 2008, and kept the belt by disqualification in a Threefold Threat with Steve Frehley and Rocky Golden in Week 4; he is booked in a Threefold Threat with Brandon James and Steve Frehley for Under Control 2008.
note: The post for this SWF Legends show reads "Wednesday, Week 2, July 2008" in its own heading; the Fry Report preview posted before it ("Wednesday, Week 4, July 2008") and the shows either side of it place it in Week 4, and this record follows them.

title: swf-generation-supreme-legends
label: Johnny Bloodstone

won.source: The Supreme Challenge 28, in-game Week 2 of July 2008 (post #300).

how: Won the belt from Chris Caufield at The Supreme Challenge 28 when the referee stopped the match as Bloodstone held the camel clutch, Caufield insisting he never submitted. He kept it against Brett Biggz on SWF Legends in Week 4 of July 2008 and against Pistol Pete Hall on SWF Legends in Week 1 of August 2008, and Robbie Retro says he has been put into a match with Bloodstone and Caufield for the belt at Welcome to the Jungle 2008. He kept it at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 in a Threefold Threat against Robbie Retro and Chris Caufield, pinning Caufield with an elbow from the top rope, and against Robbie Retro on SWF Legends in Week 4 of August 2008, when the referee stopped the match in the Bloodstone Mutilation.
note: The post for this SWF Legends show reads "Wednesday, Week 2, July 2008" in its own heading; the Fry Report preview posted before it ("Wednesday, Week 4, July 2008") and the shows either side of it place it in Week 4, and this record follows them.

title: swf-generation-supreme-generations
label: Ace Newton
how: Won the belt back from Robbie Retro in a Threefold Threat with Jay Chord on Supreme TV in Week 4 of July 2008, hitting Retro with a low blow and Chord with his finisher before pinning Retro with his feet on the ropes; in Week 1 of August 2008 the Four Kings and Playboy Jake Sawyer gave him a new belt, which Richard Eisen called the new official Generations Championship. He kept it against Kirk Jameson on Supreme TV in Week 3 of August 2008 and, in the SWF.com recaps of Generation Supreme, against El Leon and Swoop McCarthy; a match against Gino Montero for it is billed for Week 2 of September.

title: swf-generation-supreme-shooting-star
label: Marc DuBois

won.source: The diary opens with Marc DuBois as Shooting Star champion (Supreme TV, Tuesday, Week 1, March 2008); it does not date the win; dates are the diary's own in-game dates.

how: Marc DuBois's reign as the diary opens, which the diary does not date; he keeps it in ladder matches against Enygma and Antonio Marquez and loses it to Darryl Devine at The World is Watching.

title: swf-generation-supreme-sky-club-tag-team
label: High Concept

won.source: Welcome to the Jungle 2008, in-game Week 2 of August 2008 (post #467).

how: The first champions: Elmo Benson and Groucho Bling beat The Tokyo Underground at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 when Benson pinned Narato after the Game Over; the two teams had qualified for the final on SWF Legends in Week 2 of August 2008. They kept the belts against Double Deuce on SWF Legends in Week 4 of August, and lost a non-title match to Golden & Bloodstone in Week 1 of September.
